items.title: JsonPatch: allow test operations against null and empty-string values

labels.name: community-contribution
labels.description: Indicates that the PR has been added by a community member

labels.name: pending-ci-rerun
labels.description: When assigned to a PR indicates that the CI checks should be rerun

items.body:
## Behavior before 
[{
     "op": "test",
     "path": "/name",
     "value": null 
}]
applied to `{ "name": null }` fails with "The value at 'name' cannot be null or empty to perform the test operation." ## Behavior after The same patch succeeds. `test` with `null` against a non-null value, or a non-null value against `null`, fails with "The current value '...' at path 'name' is not equal to the test value '...'." ## Description The `test` operation rejects a target whose current value is `null` (JSON object and dictionary adapters) or an empty string (JSON object adapters) before comparing anything, and reports "The value at '{0}' cannot be null or empty to perform the test operation." This affects both `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson`. [RFC 6902 section 4.6 defines ](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc6902/#section-4.6)`test` as a pure equality check and lists `null` among the literals that compare equal when they are the same; empty strings compare equal under the string rule. A client that follows the spec and sends `{"op":"test","path":"/name","value":null}` before replacing a field that is still unset gets a failed patch instead of the optimistic-concurrency check it asked for. The guard is also inconsistent inside the library: `PocoAdapter` and `ListAdapter` compare null values normally, so the same patch succeeds or fails depending on whether the path resolves through a POCO, a dictionary or a `JsonObject`/`JObject`. This change removes the guard from `JObjectAdapter`, `JsonObjectAdapter` and both `DictionaryAdapter` implementations, so `test` falls through to the existing deep-equality comparison. A `null` target now matches a `null` test value, and a mismatch is reported with the existing "is not equal to the test value" message. The now unused `ValueForTargetSegmentCannotBeNullOrEmpty` resource is removed from both packages. #28021 already relaxed the dictionary adapter for empty strings in 2020; this finishes the job for `null` and for the JSON object adapters, which the System.Text.Json port inherited. #28019 reported the original problem and was closed as a duplicate of #25942, which is a different bug. * Fixes #28019 (not sure if I should open a copy when this was closed in error.) ## Nullable coercion in the Newtonsoft adapters Copilot's review pointed out that, with the guard gone, the Newtonsoft dictionary adapter accepted a `test` with `""` against a `null` `int?` entry. The cause is `ConversionResultProvider`: it round-trips the test value through Newtonsoft.Json into the target type, and Newtonsoft reads an empty string as `null` for a `Nullable` (`int?`, `bool?`, `DateTime?` and the other nullable primitives). The converted `null` then matched the `null` entry. The `PocoAdapter` and `ListAdapter` share the same helper and had no null guard, so they already behaved this way on `main`. The second commit makes the three Newtonsoft adapters compare the original test value instead of the converted one when the current value is `null`, so `null` only matches `null`. The System.Text.Json package is not affected: `JsonSerializer` refuses to convert `""` to a nullable primitive, so the conversion step fails and the test is rejected before the comparison. `test` against a `null` current value, Newtonsoft package: | Target | Test value | `main` | After first commit | After this PR | |---|---|---|---|---| | `JObject` property | `null` | fails: cannot be null or empty | succeeds | succeeds | | `JObject` property | `""` | fails: cannot be null or empty | fails: not equal | fails: not equal | | `Dictionary` entry | `null` | fails: cannot be null or empty | succeeds | succeeds | | `Dictionary` entry | `""` | fails: cannot be null or empty | **succeeds (wrong)** | fails: not equal | | `List` element | `null` | succeeds | succeeds | succeeds | | `List` element | `""` | **succeeds (wrong)** | **succeeds (wrong)** | fails: not equal | | POCO `int?`, `bool?`, `DateTime?` property | `null` | succeeds | succeeds | succeeds | | POCO `int?`, `bool?`, `DateTime?` property | `""` | **succeeds (wrong)** | **succeeds (wrong)** | fails: not equal | | POCO `string` property | `""` | fails: not equal | fails: not equal | fails: not equal | In the System.Text.Json package every `""`-against-`null` row fails with an invalid value error on `main` and after this PR, and every `null`-against-`null` row that failed on `main` now succeeds. ## Tests Added to both test projects: - `JsonPatchDocumentJObjectTest`: `test` against `null` and `""` succeeds, and mismatches in either direction throw `JsonPatchException` with the equality error message. - `DictionaryAdapterTest`: `TryTest` with a `null` dictionary value succeeds for a `null` test value and fails for a non-null one, and vice versa. - `DictionaryIntegrationTest`: end-to-end `JsonPatchDocument.Test` against a `null` dictionary entry. - `ExpandoObjectIntegrationTest` (Newtonsoft only): the null counterparts of the existing empty-string tests. Both test projects pass locally with `./eng/build.sh -test -projects ` (247 and 290 tests).

items.title: JsonPatch (Newtonsoft.Json): `copy`, `test` and dictionary keys ignore the document's `ContractResolver`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: This issue describes a behavior which is not expected - a bug.

labels.name: area-mvc
labels.description: Includes: MVC, Actions and Controllers, Localization, CORS, most templates

items.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

In `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch` (the Newtonsoft.Json-based package), #40966 (for #16690) made `add`, `replace` and `test` values go through `ConversionResultProvider.ConvertTo` with the document's `ContractResolver`. Three places still serialize under Newtonsoft.Json's defaults, so a type whose JSON form comes from the resolver (here, a contract converter it assigns) gets silently wrong results:

- **`copy`**: `ObjectAdapter.Copy` deep-copies through [`ConversionResultProvider.CopyTo`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/ConversionResultProvider.cs#L58-L79), which is `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject(JsonConvert.SerializeObject(value), targetType)` with no resolver. A type that writes `{}` under the defaults is copied as its default instance, with no error.
- **`test`**: [`PocoAdapter.TryTest`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/PocoAdapter.cs#L167), [`ListAdapter.TryTest`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/ListAdapter.cs#L184), [`DictionaryAdapter.TryTest`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/DictionaryAdapterOfTU.cs#L168) (and `DynamicObjectAdapter.TryTest`) compare `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(currentValue)` with `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(convertedValue)`, again without the resolver. Two different values that both write `{}` compare equal, so the `test` passes.
- **Dictionary keys**: [`DictionaryAdapter.TryConvertKey`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/DictionaryAdapterOfTU.cs#L211-L226) calls the public `ConvertTo(key, typeof(TKey))` overload, which passes no resolver, while `TryConvertValue` right below it passes one. An `add` to a dictionary keyed and valued by the same type converts the value and refuses the key.

The repro reads the document under settings holding an application resolver and assigns that resolver to `document.ContractResolver`, as `NewtonsoftJsonPatchInputFormatter` does. It applies the document with an error callback, as `ApplyTo(model, ModelState)` does. `Sku` is a struct whose converter the resolver assigns:

```
== 2. CopyTo, TryConvertKey and TryTest ignore the document's contract resolver
  JsonConvert.SerializeObject(sku)                -> {}
  JsonConvert.SerializeObject(sku, resolver)      -> "ABCD1234"
2a. copy (CopyTo)
  patch [{"op":"copy","from":"/sku","path":"/backupSku"}] -> sku ABCD1234, backupSku (default)
2b. a dictionary key (TryConvertKey); the value, of the same type, converts
  patch [{"op":"add","path":"/replacements/ABCD1234","value":"EFGH5678"}] -> JsonPatchError: The provided path segment 'ABCD1234' cannot be converted to the target type. (operation path '/replacements/ABCD1234', from '')
2c. test (TryTest compares JsonConvert.SerializeObject of both values)
  patch [{"op":"test","path":"/sku","value":"ZZZZZZZZ"}] -> test passed, sku is ABCD1234
```

The output is the same on 11.0.0-rc.1, and with the 11.0.0-rc.2 package.

### Expected Behavior

All three use the document's `ContractResolver`, as `add` and `replace` do:

- `copy` writes `ABCD1234` to `backupSku`. `CopyTo` could take the resolver through an internal overload, as `ConvertTo` does. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson` already passes its `JsonSerializerOptions` to both `ConvertTo` and `CopyTo`.
- The `test` fails, because the two values differ under the resolver.
- The key `ABCD1234` is converted as the value is.

### Steps To Reproduce

https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-jsonpatch-newtonsoft (section 2 of the output). It is a console app referencing only `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch`. Run it with `./repro.sh` for .NET 10, or with `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` for .NET 11 RC1. The output of both runs is committed next to it.

### Exceptions (if any)

None: each case gives a wrong result or a wrong error, with no exception.

### .NET Version

10.0.402

### Anything else?

- Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 on .NET 10. Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (and 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105) with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128. Windows 11.
- Related: #16690 / #40966 flowed the resolver into `ConvertTo` and missed these three call sites. #3498 (2018) reported the `test` half, a resolver that hid a property, and was closed for lack of community interest. #54178 is about a property-level `JsonProperty.Converter`, which is a different gap.

Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11 (10.0.26200) with .NET SDK 10.0.402, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, and with .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, and I reviewed this report.

items.title: JsonPatch (Newtonsoft.Json): values are converted under the `ContractResolver` alone, and the converter's error is swallowed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: This issue describes a behavior which is not expected - a bug.

items.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

In `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch` (the Newtonsoft.Json-based package), any `add`, `replace` or `test` value that is not already of the target type goes through [`ConversionResultProvider.ConvertTo`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/ConversionResultProvider.cs#L21-L56). That method writes the value to JSON and reads it back under `new JsonSerializerSettings { ContractResolver = contractResolver }`. Two problems follow:

1. **Every setting except the resolver is dropped.** A `JsonPatchDocument` carries only a `ContractResolver`, and [`NewtonsoftJsonPatchInputFormatter`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Mvc/Mvc.NewtonsoftJson/src/NewtonsoftJsonPatchInputFormatter.cs#L71-L74) copies only that from `MvcNewtonsoftJsonOptions.SerializerSettings`. So `Converters`, `DateTimeZoneHandling`, `FloatParseHandling`, `DateParseHandling`, `Culture` and the rest apply to a request body and not to the same value in a patch.
2. **The exception is swallowed.** The bare `catch` turns any converter error into "The value '…' is invalid for target location.". The message the converter wrote for the client is lost.

The repro reads the same JSON as a plain body and as a patch value under the same settings. It gives the patch document the settings' resolver, as the input formatter does, and applies it with an error callback, as `ApplyTo(model, ModelState)` does:

```
1d. DateTime, DateTimeZoneHandling.Utc
  body  {"shippedAt":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"} -> 2024-05-01T04:30:00.0000000Z (Kind Utc)
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/shippedAt","value":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"}] -> 2024-05-01T06:30:00.0000000+02:00 (Kind Local)
1e. a [JsonConverter] reading reader.Value, FloatParseHandling.Decimal
  body  {"price":0.12345678901234567890} -> 0.12345678901234567890
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/price","value":0.12345678901234567890}] -> 0.123456789012346
1f. a converter of JsonSerializerSettings.Converters
  body  {"discount":15} -> 15
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/discount","value":15}] -> JsonPatchError: The value '15' is invalid for target location. (operation path '/discount', from '')
1g. the exception of the contract resolver's converter
  body  {"sku":"abc"} -> JsonSerializationException: A SKU has exactly 8 characters.
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/sku","value":"abc"}] -> JsonPatchError: The value 'abc' is invalid for target location. (operation path '/sku', from '')
```

In 1e, the document itself was read under `FloatParseHandling.Decimal`, so the value reached `ConvertTo` as the exact `decimal`. The round trip under fresh settings then hands the type's converter a `double`.

For context, under Newtonsoft.Json's default settings, which `AddNewtonsoftJson()` keeps, a plain `DateTimeOffset` takes the server's offset and a `decimal` loses digits. A request body keeps both:

```
1a. DateTimeOffset, Newtonsoft.Json's default settings
  body  {"placedAt":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"} -> 2024-05-01T10:00:00.0000000+05:30
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/placedAt","value":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"}] -> 2024-05-01T06:30:00.0000000+02:00
1b. decimal, Newtonsoft.Json's default settings
  body  {"total":0.12345678901234567890} -> 0.12345678901234567890
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/total","value":0.12345678901234567890}] -> 0.12345678901234568
```

These two come mostly from `Operation.value` being read as `object` (a local `DateTime`, a `double`) before the target type is known. An application can avoid them for plain types with `DateParseHandling.None` and `FloatParseHandling.Decimal` (case 1c of the repro). It cannot avoid them for a type read by a converter (1e), because `ConvertTo` drops those settings again. #40916 (`DateOnly`: "The value '01/02/2024 00:00:00' is invalid for target location.") looks like the same mechanism.

### Expected Behavior

- A patch value is converted under the application's serializer settings, so each `patch` line above gives what its `body` line gives. One way would be for the document to carry the `JsonSerializerSettings` (or a `JsonSerializer`) and for the input formatter to set it, as it sets `ContractResolver` today. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson` already converts under the application's `JsonSerializerOptions`.
- When the converter throws a `JsonException`, the `JsonPatchError` carries its message, or at least does not hide it. Note that `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson`'s `ConversionResultProvider` has the same bare `catch`.

### Steps To Reproduce

https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-jsonpatch-newtonsoft (section 1 of the output). It is a console app referencing only `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch`. Run it with `./repro.sh` for .NET 10, or with `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` for .NET 11 RC1. The output of both runs is committed next to it; the machine's UTC offset was +02:00.

### Exceptions (if any)

None escape. The converter's `JsonSerializationException: A SKU has exactly 8 characters.` is caught and replaced (case 1g).

### .NET Version

10.0.402

### Anything else?

- Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 on .NET 10. Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (and 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105) with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128. Windows 11. The output is the same on 11, apart from the digits of 1e: 11.0 converts the `double` to `0.1234567890123456773698862321`, which is still not the client's value.
- I understand that flowing the settings needs public API on a package the docs now call legacy. #2425 (2018) asked for custom serializer settings for patching and was closed for lack of community interest. Even without new API, surfacing the converter's message would help.

Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11 (10.0.26200) with .NET SDK 10.0.402, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, and with .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, and I reviewed this report.

items.title: Adding/Removing from a collection by an index value

labels.name: area-mvc
labels.description: Includes: MVC, Actions and Controllers, Localization, CORS, most templates

items.body:
_From @gilmishal on Monday, June 5, 2017 12:34:10 PM_

I need to be able to add/remove object from a subcollection of my item - imagine the following json patch string 
`{"op":"remove", "path":"/a/b/123"}]`
or 
`{"op":"add","path":"/a/b", "value":"{"a":"b"}"`

where 123 is my database Index, and not a list position (which my client has no actual way of knowing about)

As of now, I see no way of actually implementing this (maybe I missed something, but I went through the code of both ListAdapter, and DictionaryAdapter).

If I use a Dictionary as the model, the remove operation will work, but the add will not (I could have the client send fake ids, but that would be really odd)

If I use a List as the model, well I won't be able to remove by a database Index (I could order the values in the exact same way the client does, but again - this is odd).

Implementing `IObjectAdapter` myself isn't a good option either - besides the fact that it isn't generic, and won't allow me to use multiple `IObjectAdapter`s via DI - it takes a lot of code to actually implement properly, and will basically be copying your code with minor changes.

I don't expect it to be able to actually search a list by an Id property, but I do think this entire package should be more configurable to actually allow me to define how to search a list with a given index, without copy pasting your code and applying basic changes. 

_Copied from original issue: aspnet/JsonPatch#85_
